verdict.line: You lose if Volibear lands Q's stun and chains into a healing W before your Counter Strike is off cooldown; you win almost every extended trade once Counter Strike and the free-cooldown Relentless Assault are both online.

brief.thesis: Volibear's early kit is built around short-cooldown tools — a 5-second Frenzied Maul and a sub-12-second Thundering Smash — that let him chain a stun into sustain-healing autos faster than Jax can answer with an 18-second rank-1 Counter Strike. But Jax's Relentless Assault has zero cooldown, so once both ultimates are up, every extended trade turns into an auto-attack race that rewards the attack-speed-stacker over the healer. That structural flip from short trades to long ones is why Jax holds both the lane and solo-kill edge (53.4% over 234 games) despite losing some early skirmishes.

theirWindow.when: his Q and W are both off cooldown
theirWindow.what: He'll burn Q's speed burst to close the gap and land the stunning attack, then follow with Frenzied Maul to mark you — a second W cast on that mark deals bonus damage and heals him off the exchange, so a blind all-in before your Counter Strike is ready loses the trade outright.

yourWindow.when: the instant Volibear commits his Q dash
yourWindow.what: Pop Counter Strike as he closes in — it dodges the basic attack his Q needs to land the stun, so you take nothing from the engage and stun him back instead. Follow with an Empowered Leap Strike and let Relentless Assault's stacking attack speed carry the rest of the fight.

start.why: Picked in 67% of games at 52.6% win rate — the extra trade damage and sustain outlasts Volibear's early Frenzied Maul pokes without needing to back off lane.

boots.why: Favoured 48.5% of games at 59.9% win rate; tenacity shortens how long you're locked down by Thundering Smash's stun, giving you a faster window to answer with Counter Strike or disengage.

core.why: The on-hit proc and movement speed pair directly with Empowered Leap Strike and Relentless Assault's attack-speed stacking, giving you the stat spike that wins extended trades.
Its on-hit damage and shield reward leading trades with a crit Leap Strike, which is exactly what you need to out-damage Volibear's W-recast healing.
Covers the gap when Counter Strike is on cooldown and Volibear commits a follow-up all-in — the single most common way this lane is actually lost.

situational.when: he's grouping with jungle to dive you repeatedly and you need to survive burst while fighting back
you're ahead and want to survive his all-in without spending a cooldown on it
he starts stacking health items and your flat on-hit damage stops mattering

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramps attack speed the longer you stay in a fight, stacking directly on top of Relentless Assault's own attack-speed gain — the exact resource that decides the auto-attack race against Volibear's short-cooldown W.

summoners.why: Run in 81% of games at 54.3% win rate — Ignite punishes his all-in commitments and converts your existing solo-kill edge into a secured kill, while Flash lets you reposition out of a bad Thundering Smash engage or extend one of your own.

playing.title: Bait then Counter Strike
playing.detail: Let him commit Q's speed burst at you, then trigger Counter Strike right as he's about to attack — it dodges that attack entirely, denies the stun, and stuns him back for your follow-up.

playing.title: Don't all-in without E up
playing.detail: At rank 1 Counter Strike is on an 18-second cooldown; if his 12-second Q and 5-second W are both ready while yours isn't, decline the trade and walk away.

playing.title: Open trades with Empowered Leap
playing.detail: Use W into Leap Strike to open with bonus damage, then let R take over — Relentless Assault has no cooldown, so every third consecutive attack hits harder the longer the fight runs.

playing.title: Respect the W recast heal
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul leaves a mark that heals him on a second cast — if he's already landed one W on you, disengage rather than feeding his sustain.

playing.title: Block Sky Splitter with minions
playing.detail: His E is a 1200-range lightning bolt that slows you and shields him if he's standing in the blast — use minions or terrain to eat it before level 6 rather than taking free poke.

playing.title: Punish his ult cooldown
playing.detail: Stormbringer disables nearby towers temporarily but sits on a 160-second cooldown at rank 1 — once he's spent it diving you, that's a wide window to punish elsewhere on the map.

playing.title: Force long trades, not short ones
playing.detail: Short exchanges favor his stun-into-heal combo; once Relentless Assault is online at 6, commit to 3+ auto exchanges where your attack-speed stacking and his lack of a reset win out.

brief.patchCaveat: The build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1) — only those items and runes exist in this brief. The mechanical reasoning for why each cooldown and timing matters is my own read of the kits, not measured data.
